title: Pete Crow-Armstrong Hits Three Homers in Cubs Victory Over Reds
dek: Chicago Cubs outfielder Pete Crow-Armstrong hit three home runs in the Cubs' 17-5 victory over the Cincinnati Reds on August 29, 2026. The Cubs scored six homers total in the game. Crow-Armstrong is competing in a close NL MVP race against Shohei Ohtani, who has won four MVP awards in the past five seasons.
author: The GoCheckMySports Desk
key_fact: Pete Crow-Armstrong hit three home runs in a single game on August 29, 2026, as the Chicago Cubs defeated the Cincinnati Reds 17-5.
bottom_line: Crow-Armstrong's three-homer game on August 29 occurred during an August surge that bolsters his MVP candidacy. Watch final-month performance from both Crow-Armstrong and Ohtani, and monitor voting commentary from beat writers and analysts as the season winds down to gauge whether this individual performance shifts what has been Ohtani's recent dominance in the award.
body:
Chicago Cubs center fielder Pete Crow-Armstrong hit three home runs in the Cubs' 17-5 victory over the Cincinnati Reds on August 29, 2026, according to reporting from Awful Announcing and Yahoo MLB. The Cubs scored six homers total in the game, with Crow-Armstrong accounting for half of that output.
Cubs announcer Boog Sciambi's call of Crow-Armstrong's third home run captured the magnitude of the performance: "That is drilled. Left-center field. That's back and it is gone! His third of the day!" Sciambi added of Crow-Armstrong's season overall: "He is something else. That is an MVP type season he's putting up."
Crow-Armstrong is engaged in a two-man race for the National League MVP award against Shohei Ohtani, per Awful Announcing. Ohtani has taken home MVP honors in four of the past five seasons.
After the game, Crow-Armstrong attributed the performance to a prediction from Cubs legend Sammy Sosa. "Sammy did say I was gonna hit three today," Crow-Armstrong said. "Sammy Sosa told me I was gonna hit three, and I hit three. Put that on the record."
Crow-Armstrong is recognized as one of the best defensive center fielders in baseball, per Awful Announcing. The three-home-run display paired offensive production with the defensive reputation that has anchored his MVP case throughout the season.
